questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

12 + 18 × 24 ÷ 6 – 3 = 19
questions.solution:
1) × and ÷

Given expression: 12 + 18 × 24 ÷ 6 – 3 = 19

After replacing the signs, we get:

L.H.S = 12 + 18 ÷ 24 × 6 – 3

= 12 + 4.5 – 3

= 16.5 – 3

= 13.5 ≠ R.H.S

**2) ÷ and +**

**Given expression: 12 + 18 ****× 24 ****÷ 6 – 3 = 19**

**After replacing the signs, we get:**

**L.H.S = 12 ****÷ 18 ****× 24 +**** 6 – 3**

**= 16 + 6 – 3**

**= 22 – 3**

**= 19 = R.H.S **

3) + and ×

Given expression: 12 + 18 × 24 ÷ 6 – 3 = 19

After replacing the signs, we get:

L.H.S = 12 × 18 + 24 ÷ 6 – 3

= 216 + 4 – 3

= 220 – 3

= 217 ≠ R.H.S

4) - and ÷

Given expression: 12 + 18 × 24 ÷ 6 – 3 = 19

After replacing the signs, we get:

L.H.S = 12 + 18 × 24 - 6 ÷ 3

= 12 + 432 – 2

= 444 – 2

= 442 ≠ R.H.S

Hence, ‘÷ and +’ is the correct answer

questions.question: What is the term used to describe the maximum displacement of an oscillating object from its equilibrium position?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amplitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amplitude** refers to the maximum displacement of an oscillating object from its equilibrium position.
 
• It is a measure of the extent of vibration or oscillation, typically represented in units of distance (meters) or angular displacement (radians).
 
• The amplitude is directly related to the energy of oscillation, as greater amplitude signifies higher energy.
 
• Graphically, amplitude is represented as the height of the crest or the depth of the trough of a wave relative to the equilibrium position.
 
• Amplitude plays a crucial role in determining the intensity of oscillatory motion, such as sound waves (loudness) or light waves (brightness).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency:**

 
 
• Frequency is the number of complete oscillations or cycles a wave undergoes per unit of time.
 
• It is measured in hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz equals 1 cycle per second.
 
• Frequency is inversely proportional to the period of the wave, meaning higher frequency corresponds to shorter periods.
 
• It is a key parameter in wave mechanics, influencing the pitch of sound or the color of light waves.
 
 
 
• **Phase:**
 
 
• Phase refers to a specific stage in the cycle of a wave at a given point in time, often measured in degrees or radians.
 
• It is used to describe the relative position of one wave with respect to another.
 
• A phase difference of 0° implies that the waves are in sync, while 180° implies they are out of phase.
 
• Phase is crucial in understanding wave interference, such as constructive and destructive interference.
 
 
 
• **Period:**
 
 
• The period is the time taken by a wave to complete one full oscillation or cycle.
 
• It is measured in seconds (s) and is the reciprocal of frequency (Period = 1/Frequency).
 
• The period determines the duration of one cycle and is an important factor in time-dependent wave phenomena.
 
 
 
• **Equilibrium Position:**
 
 
• The equilibrium position is the point where the net force acting on the oscillating object is zero.
 
• It represents the stable state of the system in the absence of oscillation or external disturbance.
 
• It serves as the baseline from which displacement (amplitude) is measured.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the reactivity series of metals. Which of these statements is/are correct?

**Statement I :** A piece of iron placed a solution of copper sulfate gradually develops a reddish layer.

**Statement II :** Copper is more reactive than iron and replaces it in the solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I:** A piece of iron placed in a solution of copper sulfate gradually develops a reddish layer.

 
 
• This is due to a chemical reaction where **iron displaces copper** from copper sulfate solution.
 
• Iron is **more reactive** than copper according to the reactivity series of metals, so it replaces copper in the compound.
 
• The reddish layer on the iron is due to the deposition of **copper metal** on the surface of the iron. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement II:** Copper is more reactive than iron and replaces it in the solution.
 
 
• This statement is **false**. Copper is **less reactive** than iron according to the reactivity series of metals.
 
• In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its solution. Since iron is more reactive than copper, it replaces copper in copper sulfate solution, not the other way around.
 
• *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• The reactivity series is an arrangement of metals in decreasing order of their reactivity. This series predicts how metals will react with solutions of other metals and helps explain the displacement reactions. Iron being more reactive than copper is key to this reaction.
 
• Therefore, ***Only Statement 1 is true**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of their decreasing reactivity.
 
• Metals like potassium, sodium, and calcium are highly reactive, while gold and platinum are very unreactive.
 
• In the series, **iron** is placed above **copper**, indicating that iron is more reactive than copper.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction:**
 
 
• A **displacement reaction** occurs when a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.
 
• For example, when a piece of iron is placed in copper sulfate solution, the reaction is:
 
Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu

 
 
• Iron displaces copper from the solution, forming iron sulfate and depositing copper metal.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Reactivity Series:**
 
 
• Used to predict metal displacement reactions.
 
• Helps in extraction of metals from their ores.
 
• Explains corrosion and methods to prevent it (e.g., galvanization).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reactivity of Metals:**

 
 
• Metals at the top of the reactivity series, such as potassium and sodium, react violently with water and acids.
 
• Metals at the bottom, such as gold and platinum, do not react with water or acids, making them ideal for use in jewelry.
 
 
 
• **Practical Implications:**
 
 
• Understanding the reactivity series helps in choosing suitable materials for construction and preventing corrosion.
 
• For example, zinc is used to galvanize iron because it is more reactive than iron and prevents its oxidation.

• Taxes were increased on agriculture, and land revenue was fixed at **50% of the produce**, which was collected in kind. 
 
 
 
 
• **Military Campaigns:** 
 
 
• Alauddin launched successful campaigns against **Ranthambore (1301)**, **Chittor (1303)**, and **Malwa (1305)**, consolidating his empire in northern and central India.

• Under his leadership, the Delhi Sultanate successfully repelled several **Mongol invasions**, ensuring the security and stability of his empire. 
 
 
 
 
• **Administrative Policies:**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding nutrients in food is/are correct?

A. Diseases caused by long-term deficiency of essential nutrients are called deficiency diseases.

B. Vitamin C deficiency causes rickets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A disease caused by a long-term deficiency of essential nutrients in the diet is known as a **deficiency disease**. For example, lack of vitamin D causes rickets, and a deficiency of iodine causes goiter.
 
• Statement A is correct as it accurately defines deficiency diseases, which occur due to the prolonged absence of essential nutrients in the diet.
 
• Common examples of deficiency diseases include scurvy (caused by vitamin C deficiency), anemia (caused by iron deficiency), and pellagra (caused by niacin deficiency).
 
• Statement B, however, is incorrect because rickets is not caused by a deficiency of vitamin C. Instead, rickets is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D, calcium, or phosphate, leading to weak and soft bones, especially in children.
 
• The correct answer is therefore **Option 2 (Only A)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin C Deficiency:**

 
 
• Vitamin C deficiency leads to a condition called **scurvy**, not rickets.
 
• Symptoms of scurvy include bleeding gums, fatigue, joint pain, and poor wound healing.
 
• Sources of vitamin C include citrus fruits like oranges, lemons, and limes, as well as tomatoes, strawberries, and broccoli.
 
 
 
• **Rickets:**
 
 
• Rickets is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D, calcium, or phosphate.
 
• It leads to softening and weakening of bones, primarily in children, resulting in bowed legs, delayed growth, and skeletal deformities.
 
• Sources of vitamin D include sunlight exposure, fortified dairy products, fish, and egg yolks.
 
 
 
• **Deficiency Diseases:**
 
 
• These diseases occur due to the lack of essential nutrients like vitamins, minerals, proteins, and carbohydrates.
 
• Examples include beriberi (vitamin B1 deficiency), night blindness (vitamin A deficiency), and osteoporosis (calcium deficiency).
 
• Balanced diets and supplementation can prevent such conditions.

questions.question:
Consider the following Pairs wrt. Writ issued by the Judiciary in India:

 
 

 
 **Writ**
 **Meaning**
 
 

 1.
 Habeas Corpus
 To present the person
 
 

 2.
 Mandamus
 To Command
 
 

 3.
 Prohibition
 To be certified
 
 

 4.
 Quo Warranto
 By what Authority
 
 

 5.
 Certiorari
 To forbid
 
 

How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only three pairs**__.

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

Writs

 
• The Supreme Court (under Article 32) and the High Courts (under Article 226) can issue the writs.
 
• Writs of Habeas corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo-Warranto.
 
• Further, the Parliament (under Article 32) can empower any other court to issue these writs.
 
• Since no such provision has been made so far, only the Supreme Court and the high courts can issue the writs and not any other court.

Habeas Corpus

 
• ​It is a Latin term which literally means ‘to have the body of’/to present a person. *Hence, pair 1 is correctly matched.*
 
• It is an order issued by the court to a person who has detained another person, to produce the body of the latter before it.
 
• The court then examines the cause and legality of detention.
 
• It would set the detained person free if the detention is found to be illegal.

Mandamus

 
• It literally means ‘to command’. *Hence, pair 2 is correctly matched.*
 
• It is a command issued by the court to a public official asking him to perform the official duties that he has failed or refused to perform.
 
• It can also be issued against any public body, a corporation, an inferior court, a tribunal or government for the same purpose.

Prohibition

 
• Literally, it means ‘to forbid’. *Hence, pair 3 is not correctly matched.*
 
• It is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent the latter from exceeding its jurisdiction or usurping a jurisdiction that it does not possess.
 
• Thus, unlike the mandamus that directs activity, the prohibition directs inactivity.

Quo-Warranto

 
• In the literal sense, it means ‘by what authority or warrants’. *Hence, pair 4 is correctly matched.*
 
• It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of the claim of a person to a public office.
 
• Hence, it prevents illegal usurpation of public office by a person.
 
• The writ can be issued only in case of a substantive public office of a permanent character created by a statute or by the Constitution.
 
• It cannot be issued in cases of ministerial office or private office.

Certiorari

 
• In the literal sense, it means ‘to be certified’ or ‘to be informed’. *Hence, pair 5 is not correctly matched.*
 
• It is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal either to transfer a case pending with the latter to itself or to squash the order of the latter in a case.
 
• It is issued on the grounds of excess of jurisdiction or lack of jurisdiction or error of law.
 
• Thus, unlike prohibition, which is only preventive, certiorari is both preventive as well as curative.

__
 
• **Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande** is credited with systematizing the **notation system** of **Hindustani classical music**.
 
• He compiled and categorized various **ragas** and compositions into a structured system, creating the monumental work known as the **Kramik Pustak Malika**.
 
• The **Kramik Pustak Malika** is a six-volume series, which organizes compositions (bandishes) into a logical sequence of ragas and their forms, making it easier for students and practitioners to learn Hindustani music systematically.
 
• Pandit Bhatkhande introduced a scientific approach to Hindustani classical music by analyzing the structure of **ragas**, their scales, and their performance techniques, which greatly contributed to the preservation and dissemination of this art form.
 
• His contributions modernized Indian classical music and established a standard for notating compositions, ensuring consistency across different schools of music.
 
• The Kramik Pustak Malika became a foundational text for music education in India, influencing generations of musicians and scholars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande (1860–1936) was one of the most prominent musicologists of modern India. He played a key role in reviving and systematizing Hindustani classical music.
 
• He traveled extensively across India, studying music traditions, collecting compositions, and interacting with various gharanas (musical schools).
 
• His work emphasized the scientific approach to music and aimed at making Hindustani classical music more accessible and standardized.
 
 
 
• **Kramik Pustak Malika:**

• It is used as a reference by students, teachers, and practitioners of Hindustani classical music to this day.
 
• The Kramik Pustak Malika organizes the ragas into **Thaats**, which are parent scales, making it easier to understand the relationships between different ragas.
 
 
 
• **Contributions of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Ustad Allauddin Khan:** A legendary musician and teacher, Ustad Allauddin Khan was the founder of the Maihar Gharana. He trained numerous famous musicians but did not contribute directly to the systematization of music notation.
 
• **Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar:** He was a pioneer in introducing music education to the common people. He established the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya but did not focus on music notation like Bhatkhande.

questions.question: A 640 metre long train travelling at 80 km/h overtook a 540 metre long train travelling at 72 km/h in the same direction. How long did it take the faster train to cross the other train completely?

Relative speed in m/s = 8 × 5/18 = 20/9 m/s

531 seconds = 8 minutes 51 seconds

Speed of slower train (S₂) = 72 km/h

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 
• 
 
 Train 1: 640m
 
 Train 2: 540m
 

 S1 = 80 km/h
 

 S2 = 72 km/h

 Total Distance = 640 + 540 = 1180 m

questions.question: The price of sugar is increased by 25%. What percent of consumption is to be decreased so that there would be no increase in the expenditure?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the price of a commodity increases by R%, then the reduction in consumption to maintain constant expenditure is given by:

Decrease % = [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100

Here, R = 25%

Decrease % = [25 ÷ (100 + 25)] × 100 = (25 ÷ 125) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Price of sugar increased by 25%.

Expenditure must remain the same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1015ca62d93609103ae664b693117bd03b94a619b13a139129ab2341e828cf6e.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

When Expenditure is constant, Price and Consumption are inversely proportional.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let initial Expenditure be 100 units.

⇒ Due to a 25% price increase, Expenditure rises to 125 units (assuming constant consumption).

⇒ To maintain the original Expenditure, it must be brought back to 100 units from the new level of 125 units.

⇒ Decrease required in consumption value = 125 − 100 = 25 units

⇒ This decrease must be calculated on the new base (125 units).

⇒ Percentage decrease = (25 ÷ 125) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price Reduction Rule

If the price of a commodity decreases by R%, then the increase in consumption to keep the expenditure constant is: [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100

Product Constancy Principle

When the product of two variables is constant (e.g., Price × Consumption, Speed × Time), they are inversely proportional. If one increases in the ratio a : b, the other decreases in the ratio b : a.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by A% and then by B%, the net percentage change is given by: A + B + (A × B) ÷ 100. Use a positive sign for an increase and a negative sign for a decrease.

questions.question: The cost of 3 cups and 5 plates is ₹1,080 and the cost of 2 cups and 4 plates is ₹840. Find the ratio of the cost of a cup to the cost of a plate.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 3⁸ is divided by 7?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using Fermat's Little Theorem: ap−¹ ≡ 1 (mod p) for any prime p.

Here p = 7, so 3⁶ ≡ 1 (mod 7).

We can write 3⁸ = 3⁶ × 3².

So, 3⁸ ≡ 1 × 9 ≡ 9 (mod 7).

When 9 is divided by 7, the remainder is 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 3⁸ ÷ 7

**Concept Used:**

Properties of remainders: (A × B) mod N = [(A mod N) × (B mod N)] mod N

**Calculation:**

⇒ The given expression 3⁸ can be written as (3²)⁴.

⇒ (3²)⁴ = 9⁴

⇒ Find the remainder when the base 9 is divided by 7.

⇒ 9 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 2.

⇒ Now, replace 9 with its remainder in the original power expression: 2⁴

⇒ 2⁴ = 16

⇒ Finally, divide 16 by 7 to get the final remainder.

⇒ 16 = 7 × 2 + 2

⇒ The remainder is 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fermat's Little Theorem

It states that if p is a prime number, then for any integer a, the number ap−¹ − 1 is an integer multiple of p. The formula is expressed as ap−¹ ≡ 1 (mod p).

Euler's Totient Theorem

It generalizes Fermat's theorem, stating aφ⁽ⁿ⁾ ≡ 1 (mod n) where a and n are coprime, and φ(n) represents Euler's totient function.

Successive Squaring Concept

Large powers can be calculated efficiently by repeatedly squaring the base and taking the remainder at each step to keep the numbers small and manageable.
</p

questions.question: A contractor employed 69 workers to complete a work in 20 days. How many more workers he should employ to complete the work in 12 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the constant work rule: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

69 × 20 = M₂ × 12

Total workers required (M₂) = 1380 ÷ 12 = 115

Additional workers needed = 115 − 69 = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46 workers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of workers (M₁) = 69

Initial number of days (D₁) = 20

Target number of days (D₂) = 12

**Formula Used:**

Since the total work remains constant, we use the formula: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work in man-days = 69 × 20

⇒ Total work = 1380 units

⇒ Let M₂ be the total number of workers required to complete the work in 12 days.

⇒ M₂ × 12 = 1380

⇒ M₂ = 1380 ÷ 12

⇒ M₂ = 115 workers

⇒ The contractor already has 69 workers.

⇒ Number of more workers needed = Total required workers − Initial workers

⇒ Number of more workers = 115 − 69

⇒ Number of more workers = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46 workers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule (Chain Rule)

The generalized formula for man-days calculations is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M = Men, D = Days, H = Hours, and W = Work.

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Time taken to complete a specific task is inversely proportional to the efficiency or the number of workers. More workers mean fewer days required.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in direct proportion to the amount of total work completed by the individual, or in the ratio of their efficiencies if everyone works for an equal number of days.
</p

questions.question: Find the lowest positive value of (c – b) such that the 7-digit number 1738b9c is divisible by 12.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a number to be divisible by 12, it must be divisible by both 3 and 4.

For divisibility by 4, the last two digits 9c must be divisible by 4 ⇒ c = 2 or c = 6.

For divisibility by 3, the sum of all digits (28 + b + c) must be a multiple of 3.

If c = 6, the digit sum is 34 + b. For this to be a multiple of 3, b can be 2, 5, or 8.

To find the lowest positive value of (c − b), we take c = 6 and b = 5 ⇒ 6 − 5 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The 7-digit number 1738b9c is completely divisible by 12.

**Concept Used:**

A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both 3 (sum of digits is a multiple of 3) and 4 (last two digits form a multiple of 4).

**Calculation:**

⇒ Divisibility by 4: The number formed by the last two digits is 9c.

⇒ The only numbers in the 90s divisible by 4 are 92 and 96. Thus, c = 2 or c = 6.

⇒ Divisibility by 3: The sum of digits = 1 + 7 + 3 + 8 + b + 9 + c = 28 + b + c must be divisible by 3.

⇒ Case 1: If c = 2, the sum = 30 + b. For the sum to be completely divisible by 3, b can be 0, 3, 6, or 9.

⇒ We need a positive value for (c − b), so c must be greater than b. Thus, b = 0 ⇒ (c − b) = 2 − 0 = 2.

⇒ Case 2: If c = 6, the sum = 34 + b. For the sum to be completely divisible by 3, b can be 2, 5, or 8.

⇒ For a positive value of (c − b), b can be 2 or 5.

⇒ If b = 2, (c − b) = 6 − 2 = 4.

⇒ If b = 5, (c − b) = 6 − 5 = 1.

⇒ Comparing all valid positive outcomes (2, 4, and 1), the lowest possible positive value is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is completely divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4, and divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is tripled, what is the ratio of the volume of the original sphere to that of the new sphere?

For any 3D object, the ratio of volumes is equal to the cube of the ratio of their linear dimensions.

Ratio of original radius to new radius = 1 : 3

Ratio of original volume to new volume = (1)³ : (3)³ = 1 : 27

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 27.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the radius of the original sphere be r.

Since the radius is tripled, the radius of the new sphere will be 3r.

Volume of a sphere = 4/3 × π × r³

 
 
 
• 
 r
 Original Sphere
 
 
 
• 
 3r
 New Sphere

⇒ Volume of new sphere (V₂) = 4/3 × π × (3r)³

⇒ V₂ = 4/3 × π × 27r³

⇒ Ratio = V₁ : V₂ = (4/3 × π × r³) : (4/3 × π × 27r³)

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 27

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 27.**

Surface Area of Sphere

The total surface area is given by A = 4 × π × r². The ratio of surface areas of two spheres is the square of the ratio of their radii.

Volume of Hemisphere

A hemisphere is exactly half of a full sphere. Its volume is V = 2/3 × π × r³.

Scale Factor Principle

For any two similar 3D geometric figures with a linear scale factor of k, the ratio of their corresponding areas is k² and the ratio of their volumes is k³.

__Shortcut Trick__

Numerator: (sin² 35° + cos² 35°) + (sec² 65° − tan² 65°) = 1 + 1 = 2.

Denominator: Series of cos² θ from 5° to 85° with a step of 2°.

Total terms (n) = (85 − 5) ÷ 2 + 1 = 41.

Sum of such complementary angle arithmetic series is simply n ÷ 2 = 41/2.

Required expression value = Numerator ÷ Denominator = 2 ÷ (41/2) = 4/41.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/41.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = [sin 35° cos 55° + sec² 65° + cos² 35° − tan² 65°] ÷ [cos² 5° + cos² 7° + cos² 9° + ... + cos² 85°]

**Formulas Used:**

sin θ = cos(90° − θ)

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

sec² θ − tan² θ = 1

Number of terms (n) = [(Last Term − First Term) ÷ Common Difference] + 1

**Calculations:**

**For the Numerator (N):**

⇒ N = sin 35° × sin 35° + sec² 65° + cos² 35° − tan² 65°

⇒ N = (sin² 35° + cos² 35°) + (sec² 65° − tan² 65°)

⇒ N = 1 + 1 = 2

⇒ D = cos² 5° + cos² 7° + cos² 9° + ... + cos² 85°

⇒ Total terms in this arithmetic progression of angles = (85 − 5) ÷ 2 + 1 = 41 terms.

⇒ The 41 terms consist of 20 complementary pairs and 1 middle term.

⇒ The middle (21st) term is cos² 45° = (1/√2)² = 1/2

⇒ Total Denominator D = 20 + 1/2 = 41/2

**Final Expression:**

⇒ Value = N ÷ D

⇒ Value = 2 ÷ (41/2) = 4/41

**∴ The correct answer is 4/41.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental Pythagorean trigonometric identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Complementary Angles

For any given angle θ, sin(90° − θ) = cosθ and cos(90° − θ) = sinθ. This converts paired terms into solvable identities like sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

questions.question: The ratio of the income of Ram and Shyam is 15 : 16, the ratio of their expenditure is 5 : 6, If both of them saves Rs. 10000 each, then find the amount by which the income of Ram is less than the Shyam's income.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Income ratio of Ram and Shyam = 15 : 16

Expenditure ratio of Ram and Shyam = 5 : 6

Since both save the same amount, we check the vertical difference in ratio parts.

Savings (Ram) = 15 − 5 = 10 parts | Savings (Shyam) = 16 − 6 = 10 parts

⇒ 10 parts = 10000 ⇒ 1 part = 1000

Difference in income = 16 − 15 = 1 part = Rs. 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income ratio of Ram and Shyam = 15 : 16

Expenditure ratio of Ram and Shyam = 5 : 6

Savings of each = Rs. 10000

**Formula Used:**

Income − Expenditure = Savings

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51edd0e5be8ace4bb3bdc6b5ad01f2922db138b92806e82e71812e93dea15da8.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the income of Ram and Shyam be 15x and 16x respectively.

Let the expenditure of Ram and Shyam be 5y and 6y respectively.

⇒ 15x − 5y = 10000 ... (1)

⇒ 16x − 6y = 10000 ... (2)

From equation (1):

⇒ 5y = 15x − 10000 ⇒ y = 3x − 2000

Substitute y in equation (2):

⇒ 16x − 6(3x − 2000) = 10000

⇒ 16x − 18x + 12000 = 10000

⇒ 2x = 2000 ⇒ x = 1000

Difference in income = Shyam's income − Ram's income

⇒ Difference = 16x − 15x = x

⇒ Difference = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Method

If ratio changes from a:b to c:d after subtracting S from both, then 1 unit = S(c−d) ÷ (ad−bc). It bypasses solving variables directly.

Equating Ratio Differences

When horizontal difference between ratio parts is not uniform, multiply each ratio by the gap of the other ratio's terms to make the vertical change equal.

Income-Expenditure Rule

Always remember that Income − Expenditure = Savings. Ratio problems become direct proportion problems if Savings for both entities are identically same.

questions.question: After increasing the selling price of an article by 25%, the new price of the article becomes Rs. 250 . Now a discount of 25% is offered on the new price. What would be the profit or loss in percentage on the original price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When any value is first increased by R% and then decreased by R%, there is always a net loss.

The net loss percentage is given directly by the formula: Loss % = (R² ÷ 100)%

Here, R = 25%. (The absolute value of Rs. 250 is not needed for finding the percentage).

⇒ Net Loss % = (25² ÷ 100)% = 625 ÷ 100 = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is Loss of 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price after a 25% increase = Rs. 250

Discount offered on the new price = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Original Price − Final Selling Price

Loss Percentage = (Loss ÷ Original Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/421951bbfbc4e14677dcdf1f54a64e88596ada9a2668ce73cf14a8d10ca2a7f9.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the original price of the article be x.

⇒ x + 25% of x = 250

⇒ 1.25x = 250

⇒ x = 250 ÷ 1.25 = Rs. 200

Now, a 25% discount is offered on the new price (Rs. 250).

⇒ Discount = 25% of 250 = (25 ÷ 100) × 250 = Rs. 62.5

⇒ Final Selling Price = 250 − 62.5 = Rs. 187.5

Since the Final Selling Price is less than the Original Price, there is a loss.

⇒ Loss = Original Price − Final Selling Price

⇒ Loss = 200 − 187.5 = Rs. 12.5

⇒ Loss Percentage = (12.5 ÷ 200) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is Loss of 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is successively changed by x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100. If it's an increase, use a positive sign; if a decrease, use a negative sign.

Same Increase and Decrease

If a number is increased by R% and then decreased by R%, the net effect is always a decrease (or loss). The effective loss is calculated as (R² ÷ 100)%.

Extraneous Data in Percentage Problems

In questions asking strictly for a final percentage or ratio, the absolute numerical values (like Rs. 250) are not required and can be safely ignored to save calculation time.

questions.question: (15(x²-2 x-15))/(25(x+3)(x²-25)) is equal to :

Check the given options at x = 0: Option 4 yields 3 / [5(0 + 5)] = 3 / 25

**Given:**

**Formula Used:**

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

⇒ Factorise the quadratic expression in the numerator:

⇒ x² − 2x − 15 = x² − 5x + 3x − 15 = x(x − 5) + 3(x − 5) = (x − 5)(x + 3)

⇒ Factorise the term in the denominator:

⇒ x² − 25 = x² − 5² = (x − 5)(x + 5)

⇒ [15 × (x − 5)(x + 3)] / [25 × (x + 3)(x − 5)(x + 5)]

⇒ Cancel the common terms (x − 5) and (x + 3) from numerator and denominator:

⇒ 15 / [25 × (x + 5)]

⇒ Divide the constant terms by 5:

⇒ 3 / [5(x + 5)]

**∴ The correct answer is 3 / [5(x + 5)].**

questions.question: A square and a rectangle have same perimeter. They differ in areas by 1 square cm. The length of the rectangle exceeds its breadth by
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the rectangle's length and breadth be (x + d) and (x − d) cm.

Perimeter = 2(x + d + x − d) = 4x. For the same perimeter, the square's side is x.

Area difference = Area of Square − Area of Rectangle = x² − (x + d)(x − d) = d².

Given d² = 1 ⇒ d = 1 cm.

Difference between length and breadth = (x + d) − (x − d) = 2d = 2(1) = 2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of square = Perimeter of rectangle

Difference in Areas = 1 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Area of square = a², Perimeter of square = 4a

Area of rectangle = l × b, Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b)

Algebraic identity: (l + b)² − 4lb = (l − b)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37c330bf5e12b0d603c8d816f46b0b1412fb8e85597ee9f8d1fc66562889de01.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter of square = Perimeter of rectangle

⇒ 4a = 2(l + b)

⇒ a = (l + b) / 2

For a given perimeter, a square encloses a greater area than a rectangle. So, Area of Square − Area of Rectangle = 1

⇒ a² − (l × b) = 1

⇒ ((l + b) / 2)² − lb = 1

⇒ (l² + b² + 2lb) / 4 − lb = 1

⇒ (l² + b² + 2lb − 4lb) / 4 = 1

⇒ (l² + b² − 2lb) / 4 = 1

⇒ (l − b)² / 4 = 1

⇒ (l − b)² = 4

⇒ l − b = √4 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Maximum Area for Given Perimeter

For a fixed perimeter, a regular polygon (like a square) always encloses the maximum area compared to any non-regular polygon (like a rectangle) of the same perimeter.

Minimum Perimeter for Given Area

Conversely, for a fixed area, a square has the minimum possible perimeter among all valid rectangles.

Direct Area Difference Identity

The difference between the area of a square and a rectangle sharing the same perimeter can be calculated directly using: Areaₛq − Areaᵣₑ꜀ₜ = ((l − b) / 2)².
</p

questions.question: If a, b, c are all non-zero and a + b + c = 0, find the value of (a²)/(bc)+(b²)/(ca)+(c²)/(ab).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let a = 1, b = 1, and c = −2 so that the condition a + b + c = 0 is satisfied.

Substitute these values directly into the expression: a²/(bc) + b²/(ca) + c²/(ab)

⇒ 1²/(1 × −2) + 1²/(−2 × 1) + (−2)²/(1 × 1)

⇒ −1/2 − 1/2 + 4/1 = −1 + 4 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a, b, c are non-zero real numbers.

a + b + c = 0

**Formula Used:**

If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

**Calculation:**

We need to find the value of the expression: a²/(bc) + b²/(ca) + c²/(ab)

⇒ Take the LCM of the denominators bc, ca, and ab, which is abc.

⇒ Expression = (a × a² + b × b² + c × c²) / abc

⇒ Expression = (a³ + b³ + c³) / abc

⇒ Substitute a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc (from the formula above)

⇒ Expression = 3abc / abc

⇒ Expression = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Algebraic Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

Conditional Identity

If a + b + c = 0, the first factor on the right side of the standard identity becomes zero. This eliminates the entire right-hand side, leaving a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Value Putting Strategy

For cyclic and homogeneous expressions dependent on a condition like a + b + c = 0, substituting simple non-zero integers (like 1, 1, and −2) gives the result instantly without requiring complex algebraic manipulations.
</p

questions.question: A boat can go 40 km downstream and 25 km upstream in 7 hours 30 minutes. It can go 48 km downstream and 36 km upstream in 10 hours. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Downstream speed = D and Upstream speed = U.

Given time equations: 40/D + 25/U = 7.5 and 48/D + 36/U = 10.

Multiply the first by 6 and the second by 5: 240/D + 150/U = 45 and 240/D + 180/U = 50.

Subtracting yields: 30/U = 5 ⇒ U = 6 km/h. Substituting U back gives D = 12 km/h.

Speed in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (12 + 6) ÷ 2 = 9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Downstream distance = 40 km, Upstream distance = 25 km, Total time = 7.5 hours (15/2 hours).

Case 2: Downstream distance = 48 km, Upstream distance = 36 km, Total time = 10 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed of boat in still water = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9626c507ec6d6ba68d11adba02e6430a5c699e4f307d589ddda0802fd86024d5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let downstream speed be D km/h and upstream speed be U km/h.

⇒ From Case 1: 40/D + 25/U = 15/2 ... (i)

⇒ From Case 2: 48/D + 36/U = 10 ... (ii)

⇒ Multiply equation (i) by 6 and equation (ii) by 5 to equalize the D terms:

⇒ 240/D + 150/U = 45 ... (iii)

⇒ 240/D + 180/U = 50 ... (iv)

⇒ Subtracting (iii) from (iv): 30/U = 5 ⇒ U = 6 km/h

⇒ Substitute U = 6 in equation (i): 40/D + 25/6 = 15/2

⇒ 40/D = 15/2 − 25/6 = 45/6 − 25/6 = 20/6 = 10/3

⇒ D = (40 × 3) ÷ 10 = 12 km/h

⇒ Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (12 + 6) ÷ 2 = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream & Upstream Concepts

When a boat travels along the direction of the flow of the stream, it is called travelling downstream. When it travels against the flow, it is travelling upstream.

Key Formulas

Speed of Boat in Still Water = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2
Speed of Stream Current = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

Average Speed

When a boat travels a certain distance upstream and returns the same distance downstream, the overall average speed is calculated as (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).
</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows 18% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 23%. If he gains ₹1,840 on the sale of the article, then what is the marked price of the article?

questions.question: How does the author characterize their disagreement with "ecological nativists" in the final paragraph?

As a political struggle between those who support biodiversity and those who wish to see it decline.
As an empirical dispute over what the scientific evidence actually proves, rather than a difference in environmental goals.
As a rejection of the idea that humans should have any role in dominating the planet’s ecosystems.

questions.solution:

__
 
• ***Evidence over Values.***

 
 
• The author explicitly states that their disagreements with ecological nativists are **"almost entirely about what the scientific evidence supports."** They emphasize that the conflict is **"not about values."**
 
 
 
• ***Shared Environmental Goals.***
 
 
• To prove that the disagreement isn't about values, the author lists several commitments they share with nativists: **conserving healthy species**, **finding sustainable futures**, and **retaining spaces for wildness**.
 
 
 
• ***Rejecting the "Anti-Environmentalist" Label.***
 
 
• The author clarifies that questioning established research is often mislabeled as "anti-environmentalism," but they argue this is "further from the truth" because their goal is to ensure that conservation policy is based on **empirical accuracy** rather than dogma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the author’s "alternative" to ecological nativism as presented in the text?

options.text: A "Native-Only" policy that focuses exclusively on the protection of flagship endangered species.
A "Fair Trial" doctrine where destructive measures are a last resort, regardless of an organism's origin.
The total cessation of all intervention in ecosystems to allow "wildness" to reclaim human-dominated spaces.
The reclassification of all invasive parrots as "native" to prevent further mass culls in Spain and England.

questions.solution:

__
 
• ***The "Last Resort" Philosophy.***

 
 
• The author argues that we should **"pursue coexistence, and take destructive measures only if all else fails."** This is presented as an alternative to the current "eradicate with prejudice" approach for non-native species.
 
 
 
• ***Neutrality of Origin.***
 
 
• The author calls for taking the **"same attitude towards alien ‘invaders’ that we take towards native species."** This means that the decision to use lethal control should be based on the degree of harm and the availability of creative solutions, not simply whether an animal is "alien."
 
 
 
• ***A "Fair Trial" for Organisms.***
 
 
• By advocating for "creative solutions to coexist" (similar to how we treat elephants), the author suggests that every species deserves a fair assessment of its impact before **"unnecessarily destructive methods"** are employed.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

• **Option 4**: Incorrect because the author does not suggest a literal reclassification, but rather a shift in **management attitude** that treats both groups with the same ethical and scientific rigor.

• **'Wh questions' **are questions starting with **WH words.** They include:

 
 
• **What, when, where, who, whom, which, why, how.**
 
 
 
• Questions words are used to ask about specific qualities, times, places, people.
 
• Structure of **'WH questions with an auxiliary verbs: Wh word +auxiliary verb+ subject + main verb + ?.**
 
• For example:
 
 
• **What **do you do for a living?
 
 
 
• The formation of** 'WH questions' without any auxiliary verbs: Wh word + main verb + ?**.
 
• For example:
 
 
• what happened to peter?

• The** 'interrogative sentence'** is used to form **yes/no questions.**
 
• The construction of an interrogative sentence is: **modal/auxiliary verb + subject + main verb...?.**
 
• **'An interrogative sentence' **always begins with an **auxiliary verb.**
 
• For example:
 
 
• Were the dogs barking?
 
• Do you go to school?
 
 
 
• Auxiliary verbs are helping verbs ( not main verbs).
 
• Common auxiliary verbs include** be, do, have.** Others are** will, must, shall, would, may, might, could**, etc.

Why did you write such a letter?

options.text: Why was such a letter written by you?
Why is such a letter written by you?
Why such a letter has been written by you?
Why such a letter had been written by you?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Why was such a letter written by you?'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the past simple tense and is an interrogative sentence starting with '**Why**'.
 
• In the process of transforming an active voice to passive voice, the object becomes the subject and the subject becomes the object.
 
• The tense has to be kept constant in passive voice, so '**did write**' (simple past) in active voice becomes '**was written**' in passive voice.
 
• Therefore, "**Why did you write such a letter?**" transforms to "**Why was such a letter written by you?**".

Therefore, the correct answer is- ** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
